verdict.rationale: Lium documents several product-native guards against runaway spend. At pod creation you can pick Hours, End time, or a USD Spend cap, and the pod is deleted when the limit is reached. The CLI offers `--ttl 1h` auto-removal, API keys carry server-enforced daily, monthly and lifetime USD budgets, and `lium spend` shows burn rate and runway. The 'shutdown' is pod deletion rather than a stop, but backups and volumes persist data. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that the timers and spend caps actually trigger as documented.

support.subject: As an ML engineer, I can set auto-shutdown timers or spend limits so a forgotten instance can't silently run up a huge bill

citations.quote: Pick one, and the pod is deleted when it is reached: Hours... End time... Spend cap: a budget in USD
API keys with scopes and per-key daily, monthly and lifetime USD budgets enforced by the server
lium spend                                     # burn per hour, spend per pod, runway
